question.problem:
Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(10,9)=0.7,\,F(9,5)=0.4,\,F(10,5)=0.2.
$$

Find $P(X\le 10,5\le Y\le 9).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the probability that the pair $(X,Y)$ will lie inside the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axes.

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211556/assets/a3f2d39dd5b14494c726d5bc758fb9d89c5cdc18831fc900cae68da4cf5b6dcf.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained by taking the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(10,9)$ (the blue region below) and *subtracting* the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(10,5)$ (the red region below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211556/assets/fa3c9972c42d877a17609ead70776226ab4effccc991ecece596f542efea8cad.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 10,5\le Y\le 9) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(10,9)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 10,Y\le 9)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(10,5)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 10,Y\le 5)}} \\  & =F(10,9)-F(10,5) \\  & =0.7-0.2 \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$
